99:  * Name: bchlib_flushsector
100:  *
101:  * Description:
102:  *   Flush the current contents of the sector buffer (if dirty)
103:  *
104:  * Assumptions:
105:  *   Caller must assume mutual exclusion
106:  *
107:  ****************************************************************************/
108: 
109: int bchlib_flushsector(FAR struct bchlib_s *bch, bool discard)
110: {
111:   FAR struct inode *inode;
112:   ssize_t ret = OK;
113: 
114:   /* Check if the sector has been modified and is out of synch with the
115:    * media.
116:    */
117: 
118:   if (bch->dirty && bch->buffer != NULL)
119:     {
120:       inode = bch->inode;
121: 
122: #if defined(CONFIG_BCH_ENCRYPTION)
123:       /* Encrypt data as necessary */
124: 
125:       bch_cypher(bch, CYPHER_ENCRYPT);
126: #endif
127: 
128:       /* Write the sector to the media */
129: 
130:       ret = inode->u.i_bops->write(inode, bch->buffer, bch->sector, 1);
131:       if (ret < 0)
132:         {
133:           ferr("Write failed: %zd\n", ret);
134:           return (int)ret;
135:         }
136: 
137: #if defined(CONFIG_BCH_ENCRYPTION)
138:       /* Computation overhead to save memory for extra sector buffer
139:        * TODO: Add configuration switch for extra sector buffer
140:        */
141: 
142:       bch_cypher(bch, CYPHER_DECRYPT);
143: #endif
144: 
145:       /* The sector is now in sync with the media */
146:

57:   FAR struct sdio_dev_s *dev;
58:   FAR struct inode *inode;
59:   int ret;
60: 
61:   dev = bk7258_sdio_initialize(0);
62:   if (dev == NULL)
63:     {

77:     {

80:       for (elapsed = 0; elapsed < BK7258_MMCSD_PROBE_WAIT_MS;
81:            elapsed += BK7258_MMCSD_PROBE_POLL_US / 1000)

114: int bk7258_mmcsd_initialize(void)
115: {
116:   FAR struct inode *inode;
117:   int ret;
118: 
119:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&g_mmcsd_lock);
120:   if (ret < 0)
121:     {
122:       return ret;
123:     }
124: 
125:   if (g_mmcsd_state == BK7258_MMCSD_COMPLETE)
126:     {
127:       ret = open_blockdriver("/dev/mmcsd0", MS_RDONLY, &inode);
128:       if (ret == OK)
129:         {
130:           close_blockdriver(inode);
131:         }
132:       else
133:         {
134:           ret = g_mmcsd_result;
135:         }
136: 
137:       nxmutex_unlock(&g_mmcsd_lock);
138:       return ret;
139:     }
140: 
141:   g_mmcsd_state = BK7258_MMCSD_RUNNING;
142:   ret = bk7258_mmcsd_probe();
143:   g_mmcsd_result = ret;
144:   g_mmcsd_state = BK7258_MMCSD_COMPLETE;
145:   nxmutex_unlock(&g_mmcsd_lock);
146:   return ret;
147: }

150: {
151:   int ret;
152: 
153:   (void)arg;
154:   printf("SD-NAND delayed initialization begin\n");
155:   ret = bk7258_mmcsd_initialize();
156:   if (ret < 0)
157:     {
158:       printf("SD-NAND delayed initialization failed, error=%d\n", ret);
159:     }
160:   else
161:     {
162:       printf("SD-NAND delayed initialization complete\n");
163:     }
164: }

166: int bk7258_mmcsd_schedule(unsigned int delay_ms)
167: {
168:   int ret;
169: 
170:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&g_mmcsd_lock);
171:   if (ret < 0)
172:     {
173:       return ret;
174:     }
175: 
176:   if (g_mmcsd_state != BK7258_MMCSD_NOT_STARTED ||
177:       !work_available(&g_mmcsd_work))
178:     {
179:       nxmutex_unlock(&g_mmcsd_lock);
180:       return OK;
181:     }
182: 
183:   ret = work_queue(LPWORK, &g_mmcsd_work, bk7258_mmcsd_worker, NULL,
184:                    MSEC2TICK(delay_ms));
185:   nxmutex_unlock(&g_mmcsd_lock);
186: 
187:   if (ret == OK)
188:     {
189:       printf("SD-NAND initialization scheduled in %u ms\n", delay_ms);
190:     }
191: 
192:   return ret;
193: }

462: /****************************************************************************
463:  * Name: fat_mount
464:  *
465:  * Description:
466:  *   This function is called only when the mountpoint is first established.
467:  *   It initializes the mountpoint structure and verifies that a valid FAT32
468:  *   filesystem is provided by the block driver.
469:  *
470:  *   The caller should hold the mountpoint semaphore
471:  *
472:  ****************************************************************************/
473: 
474: int fat_mount(struct fat_mountpt_s *fs, bool writeable)
475: {
476:   FAR struct inode *inode;
477:   struct geometry geo;
478:   int ret;
479: 
480:   /* Assume that the mount is successful */
481: 
482:   fs->fs_mounted = true;
483: 
484:   /* Check if there is media available */
485: 
486:   inode = fs->fs_blkdriver;
487:   if (!inode || !inode->u.i_bops || !inode->u.i_bops->geometry ||
488:       inode->u.i_bops->geometry(inode, &geo) != OK || !geo.geo_available)
489:     {
490:       ret = -ENODEV;
491:       goto errout;
492:     }
493: 
494:   /* Make sure that that the media is write-able (if write access is
495:    * needed).
496:    */
497: 
498:   if (writeable && !geo.geo_writeenabled)
499:     {
500:       ret = -EACCES;
501:       goto errout;
502:     }
503: 
504:   /* Save the hardware geometry */
505: 
506:   fs->fs_hwsectorsize = geo.geo_sectorsize;
507:   fs->fs_hwnsectors   = geo.geo_nsectors;
508: 
509:   /* Allocate a buffer to hold one hardware sector */
510: 
511:   fs->fs_buffer = (FAR uint8_t *)fat_io_alloc(fs->fs_hwsectorsize);
512:   if (!fs->fs_buffer)
513:     {
514:       ret = -ENOMEM;
515:       goto errout;
516:     }
517: 
518:   /* Search FAT boot record on the drive.  First check the MBR at sector
519:    * zero.  This could be either the boot record or a partition that refers
520:    * to the boot record.
521:    *
522:    * First read sector zero.  This will be the first access to the drive and
523:    * a likely failure point.
524:    */
525: 
526:   fs->fs_fatbase = 0;
527:   ret = fat_hwread(fs, fs->fs_buffer, 0, 1);
528:   if (ret < 0)
529:     {
530:       goto errout_with_buffer;
531:     }
532: 
533:   /* Older style MBR (pre-partition table) includes boot information for the
534:    * partition-less drive.  Check for that case first.
535:    */
536: 
537:   ret = fat_checkbootrecord(fs);
538:   if (ret != OK)
539:     {
540:       /* The contents of sector 0 is not a boot record.  It could be have
541:        * DOS partitions, however.  Get the offset into the partition table.
542:        * This table is at offset MBR_TABLE and is indexed by 16x the
543:        * partition number.
544:        */
545: 
546:       int i;
547:       for (i = 0; i < 4; i++)
548:         {
549:           /* Check if the partition exists and, if so, get the bootsector for
550:            * that partition and see if we can find the boot record there.
551:            */
552: 
553:           uint8_t part = PART_GETTYPE(i, fs->fs_buffer);
554:           finfo("Partition %d, offset %d, type %d\n",
555:                  i, PART_ENTRY(i), part);
556: 
557:           if (part == 0)
558:             {
559:               finfo("No partition %d\n", i);
560:               continue;
561:             }
562: 
563:           /* There appears to be a partition, get the sector number of the
564:            * partition (LBA)
565:            */
566: 
567:           fs->fs_fatbase = PART_GETSTARTSECTOR(i, fs->fs_buffer);
568: 
569:           /* Read the new candidate boot sector */
570: 
571:           ret = fat_hwread(fs, fs->fs_buffer, fs->fs_fatbase, 1);
572:           if (ret < 0)
573:             {
574:               /* Failed to read the sector */
575: 
576:               ferr("ERROR: Failed to read sector %ld: %d\n",
577:                    (long)fs->fs_fatbase, ret);
578:               continue;
579:             }
580: 
581:           /* Check if this is a boot record */
582: 
583:           ret = fat_checkbootrecord(fs);
584:           if (ret == OK)
585:             {
586:               /* Break out of the loop if a valid boot record is found */
587: 
588:               finfo("FBR found in partition %d\n", i);
589:               break;
590:             }
591: 
592:           /* Re-read sector 0 so that we can check the next partition */
593: 
594:           finfo("Partition %d is not an FBR\n", i);
595:           ret = fat_hwread(fs, fs->fs_buffer, 0, 1);
596:           if (ret < 0)
597:             {
598:               ferr("ERROR: Failed to re-read sector 0: %d\n", ret);
599:               goto errout_with_buffer;
600:             }
601:         }
602: 
603:       if (i > 3)
604:         {
605:           ferr("ERROR: No valid boot record\n");
606:           ret = -EINVAL;
607:           goto errout_with_buffer;
608:         }
609:     }
610: 
611:   /* We have what appears to be a valid FAT filesystem! Now read the
612:    * FSINFO sector (FAT32 only)
613:    */
614: 
615:   if (fs->fs_type == FSTYPE_FAT32)
616:     {
617:       ret = fat_checkfsinfo(fs);
618:       if (ret != OK)
619:         {
620:           goto errout_with_buffer;
621:         }
622:     }
623: 
624:   /* Enforce computation of free clusters if configured */
625: 
626: #ifdef CONFIG_FAT_COMPUTE_FSINFO
627:   ret = fat_computefreeclusters(fs);
628:   if (ret != OK)
629:     {
630:       goto errout_with_buffer;
631:     }
632: #endif
633: 
634:   /* We did it! */
635: 
636:   finfo("FAT%d:\n", fs->fs_type == 0 ? 12 : fs->fs_type == 1  ? 16 : 32);
637:   finfo("\tHW  sector size:     %" PRIdOFF "\n", fs->fs_hwsectorsize);
638:   finfo("\t    sectors:         %" PRIdOFF "\n", fs->fs_hwnsectors);
639:   finfo("\tFAT reserved:        %d\n", fs->fs_fatresvdseccount);
640:   finfo("\t    sectors:         %" PRId32 "\n", fs->fs_fattotsec);
641:   finfo("\t    start sector:    %" PRIdOFF "\n", fs->fs_fatbase);
642:   finfo("\t    root sector:     %" PRIdOFF "\n", fs->fs_rootbase);
643:   finfo("\t    root entries:    %d\n", fs->fs_rootentcnt);
644:   finfo("\t    data sector:     %" PRIdOFF "\n", fs->fs_database);
645:   finfo("\t    FSINFO sector:   %" PRIdOFF "\n", fs->fs_fsinfo);
646:   finfo("\t    Num FATs:        %d\n", fs->fs_fatnumfats);
647:   finfo("\t    FAT sectors:     %" PRId32 "\n", fs->fs_nfatsects);
648:   finfo("\t    sectors/cluster: %d\n", fs->fs_fatsecperclus);
649:   finfo("\t    max clusters:    %" PRId32 "\n", fs->fs_nclusters);
650:   finfo("\tFSI free count       %" PRId32 "\n", fs->fs_fsifreecount);
651:   finfo("\t    next free        %" PRId32 "\n", fs->fs_fsinextfree);
652: 
653:   return OK;
654: 
655: errout_with_buffer:
656:   fat_io_free(fs->fs_buffer, fs->fs_hwsectorsize);
657:   fs->fs_buffer = NULL;
658: 
659: errout:
660:   fs->fs_mounted = false;
661:   return ret;
662: }

664: /****************************************************************************
665:  * Name: fat_checkmount
666:  *
667:  * Description:
668:  *   Check if the mountpoint is still valid.
669:  *
670:  *   The caller should hold the mountpoint semaphore
671:  *
672:  ****************************************************************************/
673: 
674: int fat_checkmount(struct fat_mountpt_s *fs)
675: {
676:   /* If the fs_mounted flag is false, then we have already handled the loss
677:    * of the mount.
678:    */
679: 
680:   if (fs && fs->fs_mounted)
681:     {
682:       /* We still think the mount is healthy.  Check an see if this is
683:        * still the case
684:        */
685: 
686:       if (fs->fs_blkdriver)
687:         {
688:           struct inode *inode = fs->fs_blkdriver;
689:           if (inode && inode->u.i_bops && inode->u.i_bops->geometry)
690:             {
691:               struct geometry geo;
692:               int errcode = inode->u.i_bops->geometry(inode, &geo);
693:               if (errcode == OK && geo.geo_available &&
694:                   !geo.geo_mediachanged)
695:                 {
696:                   return OK;
697:                 }
698:             }
699:         }
700: 
701:       /* If we get here, the mount is NOT healthy */
702: 
703:       fs->fs_mounted = false;
704:     }
705: 
706:   return -ENODEV;
707: }

709: /****************************************************************************
710:  * Name: fat_hwread
711:  *
712:  * Description:
713:  *   Read the specified sector into the sector buffer
714:  *
715:  ****************************************************************************/
716: 
717: int fat_hwread(struct fat_mountpt_s *fs, uint8_t *buffer,  off_t sector,
718:                unsigned int nsectors)
719: {
720:   int ret = -ENODEV;
721:   if (fs && fs->fs_blkdriver)

727:                                                        sector, nsectors);
728:           if (nsectorsread == nsectors)
729:             {
730:               ret = OK;
731:             }
732:           else if (nsectorsread < 0)
733:             {
734:               ret = nsectorsread;
735:             }
736:         }
737:     }

739:   return ret;

742: /****************************************************************************
743:  * Name: fat_hwwrite
744:  *
745:  * Description:
746:  *   Write the sector buffer to the specified sector
747:  *
748:  ****************************************************************************/
749: 
750: int fat_hwwrite(struct fat_mountpt_s *fs, uint8_t *buffer, off_t sector,
751:                 unsigned int nsectors)
752: {
753:   int ret = -ENODEV;
754:   if (fs && fs->fs_blkdriver)
755:     {
756:       struct inode *inode = fs->fs_blkdriver;
757:       if (inode && inode->u.i_bops && inode->u.i_bops->write)

text: The local FAT guards cover the obvious mutating VFS operations, but this is still a compensating patch, not proof of SD write support. The board driver intentionally implements read-only media: status is write-protected, write commands return `-EROFS`, and `sendsetup` returns `-EOPNOTSUPP`; enabling writable FAT or BCH alone would expose commands that fail at the block layer.

752: 
753: 当前 `defconfig` 顶部注明由 menuconfig 生成。修改配置时以该文件所属配置为
754: 输入，通过 menuconfig 或 `savedefconfig` 更新，不手工维护生成的 `.config`。

756: 加入 MMCSD/SDIO 配置；`CONFIG_DMA` 是否因其他外设需要保持开启，不影响本计划，

762: CONFIG_BK7258_SDIO=y
763: CONFIG_MMCSD=y
764: CONFIG_MMCSD_SDIO=y
765: CONFIG_MMCSD_NSLOTS=1
766: CONFIG_MMCSD_MULTIBLOCK_LIMIT=1
767: CONFIG_SDIO_BLOCKSETUP=y
768: CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORK=y

771: # CONFIG_SDIO_DMA is not set

773: # CONFIG_MMCSD_SPI is not set
774: # CONFIG_MMCSD_HAVE_CARDDETECT is not set

780: 应 `select ARCH_HAVE_SDIO`，而不是把 capability 伪造为运行时功能。

thinking: **Summarizing NuttX write support and repo status****Assessing public NuttX FAT and SDIO readonly changes****Defining boundaries for public NuttX modifications****Assessing readonly config impact on csd_sdio build****Evaluating MMCSD read-only and write command handling**

text:
**Current State**

- The board configuration enables both read-only controls: [`defconfig:75`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/configs/nsh/defconfig:75), with `CONFIG_MMCSD_READONLY=y` at line 85 and `CONFIG_BCH_DEVICE_READONLY=y` at line 89. The generated configuration confirms these at [`.config:693`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:693) and [`.config:755`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:755).
- The project documentation accurately describes the implementation as 1-bit PIO, read-only MMCSD/VFAT, with no DMA, 4-bit, formatting, or writes: [`README.md:10`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/README.md:10) and [`docs/SKILLS.md:126`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/docs/SKILLS.md:126).
- `/dev/mmcsd0` is opened read-only during initialization and partition parsing: [`bk7258_mmcsd.c:55`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_mmcsd.c:55). MBR partitions inherit parent geometry through [`fs_blockpartition.c:192`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/fs/driver/fs_blockpartition.c:192).
- The self-test mounts `/dev/mmcsd0p0`, falling back to `/dev/mmcsd0`, using `MS_RDONLY`: [`periph_selftest_main.c:128`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/periph_selftest/periph_selftest_main.c:128).

**Write Path**

The public block API already supports writes through `block_operations.write`: [`fs.h:273`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/fs/fs.h:273). Writable geometry is independently advertised through `geo_writeenabled`: [`ioctl.h:809`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/fs/ioctl.h:809).

Generic SDIO MMCSD contains a complete write path:

- It always registers `mmcsd_write`, regardless of `CONFIG_MMCSD_READONLY`: [`mmcsd_sdio.c:239`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/drivers/mmcsd/mmcsd_sdio.c:239).
- Single-block writes use CMD24 and `SDIO_SENDSETUP`: [`mmcsd_sdio.c:1888`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/drivers/mmcsd/mmcsd_sdio.c:1888).
- The block write dispatcher is at [`mmcsd_sdio.c:2406`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/drivers/mmcsd/mmcsd_sdio.c:2406).
- Geometry reports `!mmcsd_wrprotected(priv)`: [`mmcsd_sdio.c:2487`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/drivers/mmcsd/mmcsd_sdio.c:2487).
- Raw MMC ioctls also expose write-capable CMD25 and CMD56 paths: [`mmcsd_sdio.c:3593`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/drivers/mmcsd/mmcsd_sdio.c:3593).

Consequently, `CONFIG_MMCSD_READONLY` is fully implemented for SPI MMCSD, where the callback is compiled out and geometry becomes false at [`mmcsd_spi.c:181`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/drivers/mmcsd/mmcsd_spi.c:181) and [`mmcsd_spi.c:1632`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/drivers/mmcsd/mmcsd_spi.c:1632), but it does not itself make the SDIO implementation read-only.

The BK7258 lower half provides the effective protection:

- It always reports `SDIO_STATUS_WRPROTECTED`: [`bk7258_sdio.c:442`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:442).
- It rejects write-data commands with `-EROFS`: [`bk7258_sdio.c:295`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:295).
- Its transmit setup is unimplemented and returns `-EOPNOTSUPP`: [`bk7258_sdio.c:566`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:566).

Therefore, write support is not currently present at the hardware lower-half level. Merely disabling the two read-only configuration options would be unsafe and would produce failed writes, not working storage.

**BCH And FAT**

`CONFIG_BCH_DEVICE_READONLY` is global, not MMCSD-specific. Opening any block/MTD node through the VFS BCH proxy has write access stripped at [`fs_open.c:196`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/fs/vfs/fs_open.c:196). BCH additionally checks both the write callback and geometry before allowing writable setup at [`bchlib_setup.c:58`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/drivers/bch/bchlib_setup.c:58), and refuses writes when its instance is read-only at [`bchdev_driver.c:320`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/drivers/bch/bchdev_driver.c:320).

The contest NuttX checkout contains a local committed FAT change, `4a67a7bad6b fix(fat): honor read-only block geometry`, which is not present in `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx`:

- FAT detects false `geo_writeenabled`, records `fs_readonly`, and mounts with `fat_mount(fs, false)`: [`fs_fat32.c:2227`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/fs/fat/fs_fat32.c:2227).
- `fat_mount()` otherwise rejects non-writable geometry when called as writable: [`fs_fat32util.c:474`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/fs/fat/fs_fat32util.c:474).
- The local state field is at [`fs_fat32.h:886`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/fs/fat/fs_fat32.h:886).
- Guards cover file open/create, write, truncate, unlink, mkdir, rmdir, and rename, beginning at [`fs_fat32.c:253`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/fs/fat/fs_fat32.c:253) and [`fs_fat32.c:1007`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/fs/fat/fs_fat32.c:1007).

There is a separate mount-flag limitation. `nx_mount()` uses `MS_RDONLY` only while finding the block driver at [`fs_mount.c:314`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/fs/mount/fs_mount.c:314); the FAT `bind` interface does not receive those flags. Moreover, NSH parses `-o` but calls `mount(..., 0, options)`, so it never sets `MS_RDONLY`: [`nsh_mntcmds.c:114`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/apps/nshlib/nsh_mntcmds.c:114) and [`nsh_mntcmds.c:209`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/apps/nshlib/nsh_mntcmds.c:209). Current protection therefore depends on read-only geometry, not an NSH `-o ro` option.

**Available Commands**

The generated build enables `cat`, `cp`, `cmp`, `dd`, `df`, `echo`, `hexdump`, `ls`, `mkdir`, `mount`, `mv`, `pwd`, `rm`, `rmdir`, `truncate`, and `umount`: [`.config:2589`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:2589). Their syntax is registered in [`nsh_command.c:160`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/apps/nshlib/nsh_command.c:160), [`nsh_command.c:293`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/apps/nshlib/nsh_command.c:293), and [`nsh_command.c:434`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/apps/nshlib/nsh_command.c:434).

`mkfatfs` is deliberately unavailable because `CONFIG_FSUTILS_MKFATFS` is unset at [`.config:2376`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:2376). The other mutation commands remain useful for writable `/mnt` RAM-backed storage, but BCH and FAT geometry protections currently prevent them from modifying SD-NAND.

**Git Implications**

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx` is detached at `4a67a7b`, one local commit beyond remote `dev-ai-contest-2026` at `dd92bcf`. The only uncommitted NuttX file is unrelated Bluetooth code: `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/wireless/bluetooth/bt_hcicore.c`.
- The project repository `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing` is clean.
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/external/README.md` is modified; `apps`, `vendor/beken`, and `vendor/openvela` contain untracked linked/overlay trees reported by `repo status`.
- No `.repo/local_manifests` directory exists. The manifest defaults NuttX to remote `dev-ai-contest-2026`: [`openvela.xml:3`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/.repo/manifests/openvela.xml:3). A fresh sync will not reproduce `4a67a7b`.

**Safe Integration**

For the current read-only product, preserve the board lower-half protections and both configuration options. Carry `4a67a7b` on a named NuttX branch and pin that branch/commit through the manifest; do not rely on the detached checkout.

For actual write support, first implement and stress-test BK7258 TX PIO, CMD24 completion, card response acceptance, timeout/cancel recovery, and read-back on disposable LBAs as specified in [`BK7258_OPENVELA_SDIO_PORTING_PLAN.md:647`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/docs/plans/BK7258_OPENVELA_SDIO_PORTING_PLAN.md:647). Only then stop advertising write-protection and disable `CONFIG_MMCSD_READONLY` and `CONFIG_BCH_DEVICE_READONLY`.

Do not add BK7258 hardware logic, fixed geometry, or board-specific mount behavior to public NuttX. The existing block, BCH, partition, and writable FAT APIs do not need modification for write support. The generic FAT read-only-geometry patch and SDIO handling of `CONFIG_MMCSD_READONLY` are candidates for separate upstream NuttX fixes, with filesystem tests and raw-ioctl coverage, rather than being mixed into the board write implementation.
